questions.stem: What is an equilateral triangle?
options: A triangle with three equal sides and three equal angles
A triangle with two equal sides
A triangle with one right angle
A triangle with no equal sides
questions.explanation: All three sides equal means all three angles are 60 degrees.
questions.teaching:
Triangles are classified two ways at once — by their sides and by their angles — and most questions test one or the other.

By sides: all three equal, exactly two equal, or none equal. Those three cases have their own names, and the one with all sides equal also has all angles equal, at 60 degrees each. By angles: one angle of exactly 90 degrees, all angles under 90, or one angle over 90. A triangle always has a name from each list, so 'right-angled isosceles' is a perfectly ordinary description. Deciding which list the question is asking about is the first step.

questions.stem: What is a scalene triangle?
options: A triangle with two equal sides
A triangle with three equal sides
A triangle with two right angles
A triangle with no equal sides
questions.explanation: Scalene means all sides and all angles are different.
questions.teaching:

questions.stem: What is a right-angled triangle?
options: A triangle containing one 90 degree angle
A triangle with three equal angles
A triangle with two 90 degree angles
A triangle with all angles less than 90
questions.explanation: Only one angle can be 90 degrees, since the three must total 180.

questions.stem: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.explanation: Hexa means six. A pentagon has five and an octagon eight.
questions.teaching:
Polygon names come from Greek number words, so learning the number words gives you the whole family at once.

Penta is five, hexa six, hepta seven, octa eight, nona nine, deca ten. You already meet several of these elsewhere: a pentagon shape in sport, an octopus with its arms, a decade of years, the Olympic pentathlon. Tri and quad cover the first two. So an unfamiliar polygon name can usually be decoded rather than recalled, which is more reliable than memorising a list.

questions.stem: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.explanation: Penta means five, as in the five-sided Pentagon building. A hexagon has six sides.
questions.teaching:

Penta is five, hexa six, hepta seven, octa eight, nona nine, deca ten. questions.stem: What is a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: Quad means four. Squares, rectangles, rhombuses and trapeziums are all quadrilaterals.
questions.teaching:
Polygon names come from Greek and Latin number words, and the prefix tells you how many sides.

Tri gives three, quad gives four, penta five, hexa six, octa eight. So identifying a polygon usually means decoding the prefix rather than memorising a list. This particular family is large and includes squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, trapeziums and kites — all sharing the same side count and differing in which sides and angles are equal. Their interior angles always total 360 degrees, which follows from splitting them into two triangles.

questions.stem: What makes a shape a square?
options: Two pairs of parallel sides only
Four equal sides and four right angles
questions.explanation: Equal sides alone gives a rhombus; right angles alone gives a rectangle. A square needs both.
questions.teaching:
Quadrilaterals form a family where each member adds a condition to the one before it, so the definitions nest.

A parallelogram has opposite sides parallel and equal. A rectangle adds that all angles are right angles. A rhombus instead adds that all four sides are equal. The shape in this question satisfies both extra conditions at once, which is why it belongs to all of those categories simultaneously — every one of them is also a rectangle and also a rhombus. Checking both conditions rather than one is what these questions test.

questions.stem: What is a rhombus?
options: A quadrilateral with four equal sides
A quadrilateral with four right angles
A shape with one pair of parallel sides
questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides but its angles need not be right angles.
questions.teaching:
Quadrilaterals are distinguished by which sides are equal and which angles are right angles.

A parallelogram has opposite sides parallel and equal. Add the condition that all four sides are equal and you get a different shape, one which keeps the parallel sides but need not have right angles — so it can look like a pushed-over square. Its diagonals cross at right angles and bisect the corner angles, neither of which is true of a parallelogram generally. Add right angles as well and it becomes a square.

questions.stem: What is a trapezium?
options: A quadrilateral with four right angles
A quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides
A quadrilateral with four equal sides
questions.explanation: The defining feature is the parallel pair.
questions.teaching:
Quadrilaterals are sorted by how many pairs of parallel sides they have.

A parallelogram has two pairs. The shape in this question has exactly one pair, so the other two sides are not parallel and may be any length — which is why it looks lopsided compared with the others. If those two non-parallel sides happen to be equal it is called isosceles. Its area formula averages the two parallel sides and multiplies by the distance between them, which follows directly from having one pair rather than two.

questions.stem: What is a translation of a shape?
options: Sliding it without turning or flipping it
questions.explanation: Translation is pure sliding — the shape's orientation and size are unchanged.
questions.teaching:
Four transformations move or resize a shape, and three of them leave it exactly the same size.

One slides the shape without turning it, so every point moves the same distance in the same direction. One turns it about a fixed point through a given angle. One flips it across a line, producing a mirror image. Those three produce an image congruent to the original. The fourth multiplies every length by a scale factor, so the image is similar but usually not congruent. Ask whether the shape has moved, turned, flipped or changed size.

questions.stem: What is a reflection of a shape?
options: Sliding it to a new position
Flipping it over a line to produce a mirror image
questions.explanation: Reflection reverses the shape across a mirror line.
questions.teaching:
Four transformations move or resize a shape, and three of them leave it exactly the same size.

One slides the shape without turning it, so every point moves the same distance in the same direction. One turns it about a fixed point through a given angle. One flips it across a line, producing a mirror image. Those three produce an image congruent to the original. The fourth multiplies every length by a scale factor, so the image is similar but usually not congruent. Ask whether the shape has moved, turned, flipped or changed size.

questions.stem: What is a rotation of a shape?
options: Turning it about a fixed point
questions.explanation: Rotation needs a centre and an angle of turn.
questions.teaching:
Four transformations move or resize a shape, and three of them leave it exactly the same size.

One slides the shape without turning it, so every point moves the same distance in the same direction. One turns it about a fixed point through a given angle. One flips it across a line, producing a mirror image. Those three produce an image congruent to the original. The fourth multiplies every length by a scale factor, so the image is similar but usually not congruent. Ask whether the shape has moved, turned, flipped or changed size.

questions.stem: What is a net of a solid?
options: A drawing of the solid from one side
A flat pattern that folds up to make the solid
questions.explanation: Nets show every face laid flat, which is why they are used for making boxes.
questions.teaching:
A net connects two-dimensional and three-dimensional geometry, which is why it appears in surface area work.

It is what you get by cutting a solid along its edges and unfolding it flat — the arrangement of faces that could be folded back up to rebuild the shape. A cube has eleven different valid ones. Their practical use is that adding up the areas of the flat pieces gives the surface area of the solid, which is far easier than trying to work with the three-dimensional shape directly.

questions.stem: How many faces does a cube have?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 square faces, 8 vertices and 12 edges.
questions.teaching:
Three-dimensional shapes are described by three counts, and it helps to be clear which is which before counting anything.

A face is a flat surface. An edge is a line where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner where edges meet. Counting is easier if you work systematically — for a prism, count the two identical ends and then the rectangles joining them, rather than trying to see the whole shape at once. Euler's rule offers a check: faces plus vertices always equals edges plus two for these solids.

questions.stem: How many edges does a cube have?
questions.explanation: Twelve edges join the eight vertices.
questions.teaching:
Three-dimensional shapes are described by three counts, and it helps to be clear which is which before counting anything.

A face is a flat surface. An edge is a line where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner where edges meet. Counting is easier if you work systematically — for a prism, count the two identical ends and then the rectangles joining them, rather than trying to see the whole shape at once. Euler's rule offers a check: faces plus vertices always equals edges plus two for these solids.

questions.stem: What is a polygon?
options: A shape with exactly four sides
A closed 2D shape with straight sides
questions.explanation: Straight sides and closed are both required, so a circle is not a polygon.
questions.teaching:
Shapes are classified before they are named, and this category has two conditions.

It must be a closed flat shape, and every side must be a straight line segment. A circle fails on the second condition, and so does any shape with a curved edge. An open figure fails on the first. Once a shape qualifies, it gets its name from the number of sides. A regular one has all sides and all angles equal; an irregular one does not, and both still belong to the category.

questions.stem: What is a regular polygon?
options: One with an even number of sides
Any polygon that is not a triangle
One with at least one right angle
One with all sides equal and all angles equal
questions.explanation: Both conditions are needed — a rhombus has equal sides but is not regular.

questions.stem: In a parallelogram, what is true of opposite sides?
options: They are parallel and equal in length
questions.explanation: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel and equal.

questions.stem: What is a vertex of a shape?
questions.explanation: Vertices are corners. Faces are the flat surfaces of a solid.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles 90, 45 and 45 degrees. How is it best described?
questions.explanation: It has a right angle and two equal angles, so it is both. Categories can overlap.

questions.stem: Which statement about a square is correct?
options: A square is not a quadrilateral
A rectangle is always a square
Every square is a rectangle and a rhombus
questions.explanation: A square satisfies both definitions. The reverse is not true — most rectangles are not squares.

questions.stem: A point at (2, 3) is translated 4 right and 2 down. Where does it land?
questions.explanation: Right increases x, down decreases y: (2 + 4, 3 - 2).

questions.stem: A point at (3, 4) is reflected in the x-axis. Where does it land?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the x-axis flips the sign of y and leaves x alone.

questions.stem: A point at (5, 2) is reflected in the y-axis. Where does it land?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the y-axis flips the sign of x.

questions.stem: Which drawing shows a 3D object with its true dimensions along three axes?
questions.explanation: Isometric drawings preserve measurements along three directions. A single view loses depth and a net shows faces flattened.

questions.stem: What is an advantage of a plan and elevation drawing over an isometric one?
options: Each view shows true measurements without distortion
It shows the object in one picture
questions.explanation: The curriculum asks for advantages and disadvantages of representations: separate views give accurate dimensions, isometric gives a single readable picture.

questions.stem: A regular pentagon's interior angles total 540 degrees. What is each angle?
questions.explanation: Regular means all equal, so 540 ÷ 5 = 108.

questions.stem: Which sequence of steps would sort quadrilaterals by their properties?
options: Check for parallel sides, then equal sides, then right angles
Check colour, then size, then position
questions.explanation: An algorithm needs decisions on defining properties. Every quadrilateral has four vertices, so counting them separates nothing.

questions.stem: Why is a square classified as a special case of several other quadrilaterals?
options: It has more sides than they do
It is the only regular quadrilateral, so it belongs nowhere else
It satisfies the defining conditions of rectangle, rhombus and parallelogram at once
questions.explanation: Classification is hierarchical: meeting a broader definition places a shape inside that group as well.

questions.stem: A shape is rotated 180 degrees about the origin. What happens to the point (4, -3)?
questions.explanation: A half turn about the origin reverses the sign of both coordinates.

questions.stem: Which combination of transformations returns a shape to its exact starting position?
options: Reflecting in the same line twice
Reflecting in two different lines once each
questions.explanation: A second reflection in the same mirror line undoes the first. Two different lines produce a rotation instead.

questions.stem: Why is 'all squares are rhombuses' true but 'all rhombuses are squares' false?
options: A rhombus meets the square definition plus more, so the second one is true
A square meets the rhombus definition plus more, but a rhombus need not have right angles
Both shapes have four equal sides, so each holds under its own definition
Squares and rhombuses are separate families, so neither statement can be right
questions.explanation: Classification statements are directional. The narrower category sits inside the broader one, not the reverse.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
questions.explanation: A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: Which property would best distinguish a rectangle from a general parallelogram in a sorting algorithm?
options: Whether the angles are right angles
questions.explanation: Both share parallel and equal opposite sides and four sides, so only the angle test separates them.

questions.stem: How many sides does an octagon have?
questions.explanation: Octa means eight, as in an octopus's eight arms.
questions.teaching:

Penta is five, hexa six, hepta seven, octa eight, nona nine, deca ten. questions.stem: What is a vertex of a solid?
questions.explanation: Vertices are corners; faces are the flat surfaces.

questions.stem: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: Two triangular ends plus three rectangular sides.
questions.teaching:
Three-dimensional shapes are described by three counts, and it helps to be clear which is which before counting anything.

A face is a flat surface. An edge is a line where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner where edges meet. Counting is easier if you work systematically — for a prism, count the two identical ends and then the rectangles joining them, rather than trying to see the whole shape at once. Euler's rule offers a check: faces plus vertices always equals edges plus two for these solids.

questions.stem: What shape is the cross-section of a cylinder cut parallel to its base?
questions.explanation: Cutting parallel to the base gives the same shape as the base.

questions.stem: What is a line of symmetry?
options: A line that divides a shape into two mirror-image halves
questions.explanation: Folding along the line makes the two halves match exactly.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explanation: Two through the midpoints of opposite sides and two along the diagonals.
questions.teaching:
A line of symmetry is a fold line: reflect the shape across it and the two halves match exactly.

Finding all of them for a shape means testing every possible fold. For a rectangle, folding through the midpoints of opposite sides works both ways, but folding along a diagonal does not — the corners miss. A square is a rectangle where the sides are equal, and that extra equality makes the diagonal folds work as well. So a square has everything a rectangle has, plus more, which is exactly where the difference between the two answers comes from.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
questions.explanation: One through each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.stem: What is a kite in geometry?
options: A quadrilateral with four right angles
A quadrilateral with two pairs of adjacent equal sides
A quadrilateral with four equal sides
questions.explanation: The equal sides are next to each other, not opposite as in a parallelogram.

questions.stem: What is a plan view?
options: The view of an object looking straight down from above
questions.explanation: Plan is from above; elevations are from the front or side.

questions.stem: What is a diagonal of a polygon?
options: A line joining two non-adjacent vertices
questions.explanation: Diagonals skip over at least one vertex.
questions.teaching:
Polygons are described using vertices and sides, and there is a specific term for a line drawn inside one.

Joining two vertices that are next to each other simply retraces a side, so it does not count. The lines that do count skip at least one vertex, cutting across the interior. They matter because they divide a polygon into triangles, and since every triangle's angles total 180 degrees, counting those triangles gives you the angle sum of any polygon. A quadrilateral splits into two, a pentagon into three, and so on.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 5, 5 and 8 cm. How is it classified?
questions.explanation: Exactly two sides are equal.

questions.stem: A point at (1, 6) is translated 3 left and 4 down. Where does it land?
questions.explanation: Left decreases x and down decreases y.

questions.stem: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are equal in length?
questions.explanation: Rectangles and squares have equal diagonals; rhombuses have perpendicular but unequal ones.

questions.stem: What does a net of a cube consist of?
options: Six squares arranged so they fold into a cube
questions.explanation: There are eleven distinct nets that fold correctly into a cube.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of all parallelograms?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles and opposite sides are equal, but the other properties belong to special cases.

questions.stem: A regular octagon's interior angles total 1080 degrees. What is each angle?
questions.explanation: Regular means equal, so 1080 ÷ 8 = 135.

questions.stem: Which transformation would map a shape onto its mirror image?
questions.explanation: Only reflection reverses orientation.

questions.stem: Why is an isometric drawing useful for a builder?
options: It shows three faces at once, giving a clear sense of the whole object
It shows exact angles without distortion
questions.explanation: It trades angular accuracy for a readable single image, which is why plans accompany it.

questions.stem: Why does reflecting a shape twice in parallel lines produce a translation?
options: It returns the shape to its start
The two reversals cancel, leaving a shift equal to twice the distance between the lines
questions.explanation: Orientation is restored after two reflections, and the net effect is a slide.

questions.stem: A shape has rotational symmetry of order 4. What does this mean?
options: It looks identical four times during a full turn
It has four lines of symmetry
It can be rotated only four times
questions.explanation: Order counts how many positions in one full rotation look the same.

questions.stem: Which property distinguishes a square from every other rhombus?
questions.explanation: All rhombuses share the other three properties; only the square adds right angles.

questions.stem: Why does a 3D object drawn on paper always lose some information?
options: Three dimensions must be represented in two, so something is compressed or hidden
Two dimensions cannot show curved surfaces
Drawings must use a smaller scale than the object
Only colour and texture are lost, not shape
questions.explanation: Every projection is a trade-off, which is why engineers use multiple views together.

questions.stem: How many sides does a decagon have?
questions.explanation: Deca means ten, as in a decade of ten years. A dodecagon has twelve sides.

questions.stem: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: Three on each triangular end plus three joining them.
questions.teaching:
Three-dimensional shapes are described by three counts, and it helps to be clear which is which before counting anything.

A face is a flat surface. An edge is a line where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner where edges meet. Euler's rule offers a check: faces plus vertices always equals edges plus two for these solids.

questions.stem: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
questions.explanation: Four at the base corners plus one apex.

questions.stem: What is a cross-section?
options: The shape revealed when a solid is cut through
questions.explanation: A prism has the same cross-section along its length.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
questions.explanation: One horizontal and one vertical through the midpoints; the diagonals are not lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: What is an elevation drawing?
options: A view of an object from the front or side
questions.explanation: Plan is from above; elevations are from the sides.

questions.stem: What is a prism named after?
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has triangular ends, a hexagonal prism hexagonal ones.

questions.stem: What is a congruent shape?
options: A shape with the same area only
A shape with the same perimeter only
A larger copy of a shape
A shape identical in size and shape to another
questions.explanation: Congruent shapes match exactly, possibly after rotation or reflection.

questions.stem: What is a similar shape in geometry?
options: The same shape but a different size
Exactly the same size and shape
A shape with the same area
questions.explanation: Similar shapes have equal angles and proportional sides.

questions.stem: A point at (-2, 5) is reflected in the x-axis. Where does it land?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the x-axis reverses the sign of y.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
questions.explanation: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides.

questions.stem: Why is a square also a rectangle?
options: It has four right angles, which is the rectangle definition
questions.explanation: Meeting a broader definition places a shape inside that category.

questions.stem: A net has six identical squares. Which solid does it fold into?
options: A rectangular prism with different faces
questions.explanation: Six equal squares can only form a cube, provided they are arranged correctly.

questions.stem: Which transformation moves every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction?
questions.explanation: A translation slides the whole shape uniformly. Under rotation and reflection, different points move different distances, and enlargement changes the distances between points.

questions.stem: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a rectangle?
questions.explanation: It looks the same after a half turn and after a full turn.

questions.stem: Which pair of shapes must be similar?
questions.explanation: All circles have the same shape, so any two are similar. Rectangles can differ in proportion.

questions.stem: Why do two triangles with equal angles have to be similar?
options: Equal angles fix the shape, so the sides must be in proportion
They must also have equal sides
questions.explanation: Angle-angle is a sufficient condition for similarity in triangles.

questions.stem: A shape is reflected in the y-axis then in the x-axis. What single transformation is equivalent?
options: A reflection in the line y = x
A rotation of 180 degrees about the origin
questions.explanation: Both coordinates change sign, which is exactly a half turn about the origin.

questions.stem: Why does an isometric drawing keep vertical lines vertical but slant the others?
options: It is an error in the technique
It represents depth on a flat page while keeping height readable
questions.explanation: The convention trades true angles for a readable impression of three dimensions.

questions.stem: Which property is shared by all parallelograms but not by all trapeziums?
options: Its diagonals are equal in length
It has at least one pair of parallel sides
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel
Its opposite angles add to 180 degrees
questions.explanation: A trapezium needs only one parallel pair.

questions.stem: A sorting algorithm asks 'four sides?', then 'all angles equal?', then 'all sides equal?'. What does it identify at the end?
questions.explanation: Four sides plus equal angles gives a rectangle; adding equal sides narrows it to a square.
